title: Sr IT Engineer
desc:
Sr IT Engineer
Location: Miami, FL
Status: Full-Time / Exempt
About eMed
The GLP-1 era didn't create America's metabolic crisis. It just made it impossible to look away. Roughly 90% of U.S. healthcare spending goes to chronic disease that begins in metabolism, and for decades the system's answer was to wait for a massive health issue, then send the bill. eMed was built to get there first.
We are at the epicenter of healthcare transformation an AI enabled platform. We put diagnostic-grade blood testing on people's kitchen tables, clinicians on their screens in minutes, and real biomarkers at the center of every decision.
Today we offer GLP-1 management, where employers facing double-digit cost increases need programs that actually work. That's where we're winning. It is not where we stop. Cardiometabolic risk gets caught years before it becomes a claim that's we're building. If you've spent your career watching healthcare treat consequences, come help us treat causes.
Purpose of Role
Technology is changing how we manage chronic conditions. At eMed we're building the platform leading that shift: reducing the cost of care while increasing its quality. The Senior IT Engineer designs, builds, and supports the company’s hardware, software, network infrastructure, and SaaS ecosystem. This position is responsible for architecting scalable and secure systems, monitoring network health, leading infrastructure projects, ensuring robust data protection, and resolving complex technical issues across our growing environment.
What You Will Work On
Serve as a technical architect for the company’s SaaS ecosystem, designing and implementing integrations that connect SaaS applications into cohesive, secure workflows
Design, manage, and troubleshoot network infrastructure (LAN/WAN, Wi-Fi, VPN, firewalls, switching, and routing), with a strong understanding of core networking concepts (TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VLANs)
Monitor network health and performance, proactively identifying and resolving connectivity and system issues
Collaborate with the Security team to implement and maintain system security controls (e.g., user authorization, firewalls, endpoint protection)
Collaborate with the Cloud/Infrastructure team to design, deploy, and support scalable hybrid and cloud environments
Manage installations, upgrades, and configurations of hardware and software
Administer and support VMware Workspace ONE for device enrollment, configuration, application deployment, and policy management
Assess system performance and recommend and implement improvements
Ensure data is handled, transferred, and processed according to legal and company guidelines
Provide escalation support and guidance to stakeholders and help desk staff, and mentor team members on technical best practices
Develop and deliver training and documentation to end users on systems, tools, and security best practices
Effectively navigate complex software licensing models and ensure the company is strategic in its SaaS purchasing, usage, and renewals
Manage contracts with vendors (e.g., development platforms, telecommunication companies, password managers) and software licenses
Manage devices and password management tools
Develop and maintain IT policies, standards, and procedures
Configure and manage SSO (Active Directory, Okta, AWS)
Manage assets and IT inventory
Manage change management processes and communications
Participate in incident response and perform root cause analysis as needed
What We're Looking For
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or relevant field experience
8+ years of experience in IT Operations, with at least 3 years in a leadership role
Strong experience with system installation, configuration, analysis, and data protection operations and legislation (e.g., GDPR)
Thorough knowledge of core networking concepts (TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VLANs), cloud computing, and single sign-on (Active Directory, Okta, AWS)
Excellent leadership, organizational, problem-solving, and communication skills to manage multiple projects and mentor team members
Our Stack
VMware Workspace ONE, Active Directory, Okta, AWS, TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VLANs, LAN/WAN, Wi-Fi, VPN, Firewalls, Switching, Routing, and SaaS management tools.
Perks at Work
Health Care Plan (Medical, Dental & Vision)
Retirement Plan (401k with Company Match)
Life Insurance (Basic, Voluntary & AD&D)
Paid Time Off
Short Term & Long Term Disability
Training & Development
Catered breakfast and lunch daily, snacks
Wellness Resources

title: Systems Analyst and Database Administrator
desc:
About Us

Think BIG. Achieve More.

At City National Bank of Florida, we invest in our people and the communities we serve. Join a team where ambitious careers and meaningful relationships thrive together. We’re entrepreneurs at heart—growing fast, making an impact, and shaping the future of banking in Florida. To learn more about City National Bank of Florida visit About Us!

Overview

The Systems Analyst & Database Administrator is responsible for administering, monitoring, supporting, and continuously improving the Bank’s on-premises and cloud database environments. The position serves as a primary technical resource for database availability, performance, capacity, security, patching, backup, recovery, production support, and service restoration across business-critical data platforms.

The role also administers and supports the Power BI environment and Gateway infrastructure, including data source connections, credentials, configuration changes, refresh connectivity, platform monitoring, and technical support required for successful report deployments. The position works closely with Data Operations, Data Engineering, Data Architecture, Information Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, application support teams, vendors, and business stakeholders to resolve operational issues, implement changes, improve early-warning capabilities, and ensure reliable delivery of enterprise data services.

The incumbent applies systems-analysis techniques to evaluate operational requirements, troubleshoot complex technical issues, document solutions, and identify opportunities to automate repetitive activities, modernize legacy components, and improve operational resiliency.

What You'll Do

Applies systems analysis techniques and procedures to determine hardware, software, database, and system requirements that support business and operational needs. 
Administers and maintains enterprise database platforms across on-premises and cloud environments, ensuring reliability, performance, security, and availability. 
Monitors database health, performance, capacity, storage utilization, and operational processing activities to identify and resolve issues that could affect service delivery. 
Independently investigates and resolves database-related incidents, service requests, production issues, and operational exceptions within established service levels. 
Performs database performance analysis and tuning, including optimization of queries, indexes, stored procedures, database objects, and configurations. 
Plans, coordinates, tests, and implements database maintenance activities, including software upgrades, patches, configuration changes, and platform enhancements. 
Maintains and tests database backup, recovery, disaster recovery, and service restoration procedures to support business continuity and operational resiliency. 
Administers and supports Power BI environment components, including Gateway infrastructure, data source configurations, credentials, connectivity, and deployment dependencies. 
Provides operational support for Power BI solutions by troubleshooting environment, connectivity, refresh, Gateway, and platform-related issues and coordinating resolution with the appropriate teams. 
Supports database, reporting, integration, and data platform initiatives by translating business and technical requirements into operational solutions. 
Participates in database migrations, system implementations, data conversions, infrastructure changes, and technology modernization efforts. 
Collaborates with Data Operations, Data Engineering, Data Architecture, Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, vendors, and business stakeholders to support enterprise data services. 
Supports operational monitoring, process integrity validation, and early detection of failures affecting databases, integrations, reporting environments, and other data services. 
Participates in automation and continuous improvement initiatives that improve monitoring, reliability, operational efficiency, early-warning capabilities, and service delivery. 
Implements production changes in accordance with established change management, testing, approval, documentation, evidence retention, and rollback requirements. 
Maintains technical procedures, operational runbooks, knowledge articles, recovery plans, implementation records, system inventories, and supporting documentation. 
Provides technical support for audits, regulatory reviews, risk assessments, control testing, evidence requests, and remediation efforts. 
Supports database security, access management, data protection controls, and compliance with applicable security, privacy, and regulatory requirements. 
Evaluates database technologies, administration tools, monitoring platforms, vendor solutions, and automation opportunities that improve operational effectiveness and reliability. 
Participates in integration and orchestration improvements intended to reduce repetitive work, modernize legacy processing, and improve detection and recovery when processes fail. 
Participates in on-call, after-hours, weekend, holiday, maintenance, and recovery activities as required to support critical enterprise data services. 
Performs other related duties as assigned in support of Enterprise Data Management objectives and operational service delivery. 


Qualifications

5-7 years of progressive experience in systems analysis and database administration. 
5-7 years experience administering and supporting Microsoft SQL Server environments in production. 
3-5 years experience support database performance tuning, backup and recovery, disaster recovery, patch management, and production support. 
Experience troubleshooting database, application, and connectivity issues in complex enterprise environments. 
Experience supporting production incidents, service requests, operational monitoring, and service restoration activities. 
Experience with T-SQL development, query optimization, stored procedures, functions, views, indexes, and database maintenance activities. 
Experience supporting Power BI, SQL Reporting Services, SSIS, Azure Data Factory, or similar reporting and data integration technologies. 
Experience with data analysis, data modeling, data warehouse concepts, and reporting environments .
Experience in banking, financial services, or other regulated industries.


Education

Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field.
An equivalent combination of education and/or relevant professional experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.

We offer a competitive benefits package designed to support your success:

Health Coverage: Medical, dental, and vision plans with employer contributions.
Retirement Savings: 401(k) with matching.
Paid Time Off & Holidays: Generous PTO and paid holidays.
Wellness Support: Access to mental health and financial wellness resources.

Job Title: IT Manager


Location: South Florida (100% in office, not hybrid / remote)

IT Manager Position Overview


We are on the lookout for a skilled IT Manager who will play a crucial role in the ongoing support and enhancement of our organization's technological landscape. This pivotal position is designed for someone who is not only adept at managing IT systems but also passionate about driving improvements that elevate overall business operations through efficient IT solutions. Deliver comprehensive technical support to end users, addressing a wide range of issues related to hardware, software, and network connectivity.

Troubleshoot a diverse array of devices including desktops, laptops, printers, and mobile technology, ensuring minimal downtime and swift resolution of issues.
Maintain thorough documentation of systems, IT standards, and technology best practices, contributing to continuous improvement in operations.
Engage with team members to identify potential areas for enhancing systems, refining processes, and boosting overall IT efficiency.
Provide training and technical guidance to users as needed, empowering them to leverage technology effectively in their roles.


**Qualifications and Experience**
Bilingual in English and Spanish preferred
A minimum of 5 years of experience in IT administration or management, with a solid background in systems administration and infrastructure support.
Extensive knowledge of the Microsoft Windows environment, including Active Directory, networking principles, and Microsoft 365 services.
Proven experience in supporting various IT functions, including server management, virtualization, backup solutions, security measures, and endpoint management.
Strong troubleshooting skills across a broad range of hardware and software, enabling effective resolution of diverse technical issues.
Experience collaborating with vendors to facilitate technology implementations, ensuring they meet organizational needs.
Exceptional communication, organizational, and problem-solving abilities are essential for success in this role.
A Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field is preferred; however, equivalent practical experience will also be considered.

Experience with cloud technologies such as Azure and/or AWS.
Understanding of virtualization platforms and their applications in a business context.
Experience in providing VPN and remote access support.
Knowledge of network security concepts and their implementation.
Previous experience with ERP systems or other enterprise business applications would be advantageous.


This role presents a unique opportunity to be integral to the support and advancement of a dynamic organization’s technology framework. You will engage in a variety of infrastructure and business technology initiatives, making a significant impact as we continue to grow and innovate.

title: Systems Administrator I
desc:
About Switch

At Switch, we don’t just design, build and operate data centers—we are enabling the technology of the future. Led by Founder & CEO, Rob Roy, we believe in revolutionary innovation, operational excellence and the principle of karma. Switch is where talented people come together to EVOLVE the digital world.

We believe that innovation isn’t just about technology—it’s about the people, culture, and purpose that make it happen. Every Switch team member contributes to a mission greater than themselves: to create the world’s most advanced digital infrastructure that powers the progress of humanity.

The Role: Systems Administrator I

As a Systems Administrator I at Switch, you will administer and support enterprise technology systems after issues move beyond frontline Service Desk support. You will troubleshoot incidents, perform maintenance and production changes, and help keep assigned systems secure, available, and reliable. You will work independently on routine and moderately complex issues using established standards and procedures. You will escalate issues that require advanced expertise.

What You’ll Do

Administer, monitor, maintain, and troubleshoot assigned enterprise systems, applications, and infrastructure services.
Provide Tier-2 support for incidents and service requests, maintaining ownership through resolution or appropriate escalation.
Diagnose system, application, authentication, connectivity, performance, capacity, and configuration issues.
Respond to monitoring alerts and service disruptions, take corrective action, and confirm service restoration.
Perform patching, upgrades, vulnerability remediation, certificate management, configuration changes, and other system maintenance.
Prepare, document, peer review, and execute routine production changes using established change-management procedures.
Use scripting, automation, and configuration-management tools to improve routine administrative work.
Support access management, security, audit, and compliance requirements for assigned systems.
Create and maintain technical procedures, runbooks, and knowledge articles.
Contribute technical work to implementations, migrations, and other technology projects.
Participate in the rotating on-call schedule and provide after-hours support for escalated incidents when required.
Maintain reliable transportation and be able to work onsite at a Switch data center when needed.


What We’re Looking For

You troubleshoot methodically and use logs, alerts, errors, and other diagnostic information to identify problems.
You make sound decisions within established procedures and know when an issue needs to be escalated.
You communicate technical information clearly and include the details others need to act.
You follow production, security, and change-management procedures consistently.
You take ownership of assigned work and follow issues through resolution.
You share useful documentation and technical knowledge with the team.
You work effectively with other IT teams, technical specialists, and vendors when an issue crosses areas of responsibility.


What You’ll Bring

2–4 years of relevant experience in systems administration, infrastructure operations, enterprise application administration, or a related technical area, or an equivalent combination of experience and technical training.
Hands-on experience administering and troubleshooting enterprise technology in a production environment.
Working knowledge of Windows Server and/or enterprise Linux.
Foundational knowledge of networking, identity and access management, virtualization, backup and recovery, monitoring, and information security.
Experience with relevant technologies such as Active Directory or Microsoft Entra ID, DNS and DHCP, Microsoft 365 or Exchange, virtualization, enterprise backup and monitoring platforms, or certificate management.
Experience with PowerShell, Bash, Python, Ansible, or another scripting or automation technology.
Familiarity with IT service management and production change-management practices.
Relevant technical education, training, or certifications are helpful but not required. This may include college coursework, technical school, military technical training, apprenticeships, vendor training, or industry certifications.
If your experience does not match every item above, we encourage you to apply if your background prepares you to perform the core responsibilities of the role.


Why Switch?

A Culture of Karma – We are self-motivated by karma, ensuring our actions contribute to a positive, supportive and forward-thinking environment.
Industry Leading Designs – Work with the most advanced data center technology on the planet and be a part of emerging technology development.
Flexibility & Remote Opportunities – Whether in-office, hybrid, or fully remote, we offer the technology and support to keep teams connected and productive.
Career Stability & Growth – In this expanding industry, we invest in our people, providing opportunities & advancement in a stable, growing company.
Generous Benefits Package - Switch provides comprehensive coverage for you and your family that can be tailored to fit your personal needs, and more!


Join Us & Make a Difference

This is more than a job—it’s a mission. If you’re ready to be part of a culture that values innovation, karma, and limitless potential, we want to hear from you.

Apply Now and Let’s Build the Future Together.

Applicant and Candidate Privacy Notice

Your privacy rights may vary by location. Learn more in our Switch Applicant and Candidate Privacy Notice https://www.switch.com/applicant-and-candidate-privacy/ to understand how Switch collects, uses, shares, and protects your personal information during the recruiting process.

Safe Hiring Notice

Legitimate Switch recruiting emails come from switch.com. Current opportunities are posted on https://switch.com/careers and the official Switch LinkedIn Company page https://www.linkedin.com/company/switch-data-centers/. Switch will never ask you to pay fees, purchase equipment, send money, cash a check, or transfer funds as part of recruiting. Personal information is collected only through approved Switch systems.

If you suspect recruiting fraud, stop communicating with the sender and review FTC guidance https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/what-do-if-you-were-scammed.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Switch is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We provide employment opportunities without discrimination or harassment based on any characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Accommodations

Switch provides reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities throughout the hiring process. If you need an accommodation, contact careers@switch.com.

Switch also considers qualified applicants with criminal histories in accordance with applicable law.

Recruitment Agencies

Switch does not accept unsolicited resumes or candidate submissions from agencies without a current written agreement. Switch is not responsible for fees related to unsolicited submissions.

title: Senior Systems Administrator - South San Francisco, California
desc:
At Slipstream Life Sciences we work to streamline IT Support and provide managed solutions with a strategic consulting and global leadership management approach. Our solutions are designed exclusively for emerging pharma and biotech organizations.

Slipstream’s industry-leading solutions free clients from the demands of internal IT and allow them to rapidly advance their mission. Led by a leadership team that has been together for over 10 years, you will join a proven team, culture, and strategy to drive innovation within the IT outsourcing industry while developing your skillset with the opportunities for internal growth.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a Senior IT Systems Engineer to be the technical lead for our Windows server and directory services and for the IT side of laboratory computing. You will partner stakeholders in lab operations, automation and software engineering to keep the computers that support our research secure, patched, and integrated with the rest of our environment. You will be the escalation point for corporate IT architecture and Windows systems issues, support colleagues across functions, and help the IT team mature its processes and governance.

This role calls for strong technical judgment and excellent communication. We are looking for someone with experience applying practices and standards to raise the bar for how we operate. You will get results through effective communication, and the ability to anticipate needs that your colleagues may not have realized. You will balance textbook operational practice against what is practical for a fast-moving research organization.

The position is onsite in our South San Francisco office, and occasional evening and weekend work is required.

What You Will Do

Windows and Laboratory Computing

Administer our Windows server and directory environment, including Active Directory, Group Policy, and system hardening.
Support the storage, networking, and PC management that laboratory computing depends on.
Partner with laboratory operations and automation teams to onboard, patch, secure, and integrate instruments and complex workcells computers.
Maintain accurate records of hardware and software assets through their lifecycle, including licensing, maintenance, and replacement.
Participate in the on-call rotation for critical IT issues.


Change vetting and incident response

Review incoming projects with laboratory and research stakeholders, assess the operational impact of proposed changes (for example, authentication changes or new system rollouts), and define testing and mitigation plans before work begins.
Investigate the root cause of critical incidents and recommend changes that prevent recurrence.


Security, governance, and operational maturity

Contribute to security procedures and governance as the company scales and to meet compliance requirements.
Triage and remediate vulnerability findings on the Windows, directory, and laboratory computing systems you support, working with security and partner teams on prioritization and timelines.
Define, apply, and maintain secure configuration baselines for Windows servers, directory services, and laboratory computers, and verify that systems stay in compliance with them.
Drive continual improvement of endpoint management, application deployment, and security configuration.
Identify and implement process improvements and automation, using PowerShell or other scripting tools to streamline common tasks.
Manage vendor relationships and evaluate vendor performance for IT equipment, software, and services.
Support business continuity by aligning IT systems with our resilience strategy.


Working Across Functions

Serve as the escalation point for corporate IT architecture and lab Windows issues, and help colleagues across IT and partner teams work complex technical problems through to resolution.
Set clear goals for yourself and for project teams, and give regular updates on delivery.
Build trust with stakeholders through active listening, and use influence and persuasion to align teams on the right approach.
Anticipate needs that colleagues have not yet recognized and bring forward solutions early.
Bring forward recommendations grounded in your experience, with the tradeoffs and risks laid out, so that decisions can be made on evidence.
Create and maintain functional and operational documentation to a consistent quality standard, and design and deliver training that raises the skills of the IT team and the colleagues we support.
Own complex projects and workstreams from requirements through delivery, and produce the plans, system diagrams, and technical specifications for your own projects and for others.
Apply continual improvement practices for existing architectures including Windows and directory services and for the IT systems that support laboratory computing, with a long-term view of maintainability and technical debt.
Understand the business and technical needs of the laboratory, research computing, and corporate functions you support, and design solutions to fit them.
Plan and execute technology upgrades so they stay compatible with existing systems and cause minimal disruption.


About You

You have a bachelor's degree and 8 or more years of relevant experience, and/or advanced education or certification, ideally as a senior systems engineer or technical lead in a biotechnology or medtech lab environment.
You have deep, hands-on experience with Windows Server, Active Directory, Group Policy, and system hardening, plus working knowledge of storage and networking.
You have experience triaging vulnerability findings and maintaining secure configuration baselines, and you can explain the risk behind a finding to colleagues who are not security specialists.
You have written technical specifications and architecture documents for complex projects, and you think ahead about maintainability and technical debt.
You define your own work. You identify what needs doing, set goals for yourself and for project teams, build the plan, and get results without formal authority or waiting for direction.
You make recommendations from experience and from current knowledge of the field, and you back them with reasoning that colleagues can evaluate.
You are a strong communicator in writing and in person. You explain highly technical information clearly to technical and nontechnical colleagues, and you build trusted relationships across functions and levels, including with scientists and lab staff.
You develop clear project plans and system diagrams, and you hold documentation to a quality standard so that it stays accurate, current, and usable by others.
You listen actively and anticipate needs that others have not yet recognized.
You make sound decisions under ambiguity and know when a practical solution is better than the textbook one.
You handle confidential information with discretion.
You are committed to continual improvement through your own learning and development, and you want to leave the IT program stronger than you found it.


Nice to Have

Experience with cloud productivity suites, cloud endpoint management, single sign-on and identity providers, or Windows workloads in a public cloud, held to the same patching, monitoring, and security standards as on-premises systems.
Experience supporting endpoints and mobile device management in a mixed Mac and Windows environment.
Tooling and scripting: experience with enterprise system management and monitoring tools, and scripting or automation in PowerShell, Python, or Bash.
Regulated environments: experience in regulated laboratory or biotech settings, with familiarity with relevant security frameworks and regulatory requirements.
Certifications: relevant IT certifications.


Benefits

401k match
Comprehensive group health, dental, vision benefits
Life insurance/LTD
Discretionary PTO
Salary: $135,000-$145,000

desc:
Company Description

Integrated Dermatology is a leading national dermatology practice that acquires and partners with dermatology practices across the United States. The culture at ID is a reflection of its people. Position Summary

The Systems Engineer, Practice Operations leads the technical assessment, planning, remediation, implementation, and validation work required to transition acquired and existing practices to Integrated Dermatology standards.

This position serves as the subject matter expert for SonicWall firewalls, Ubiquiti networking, practice connectivity, and site infrastructure. The Systems Engineer works directly with practice leadership, internal teams, carriers, vendors, cabling providers, and managed service providers to deliver standardized, secure, supportable practice environments. The position also leads Microsoft 365 tenant and data migrations associated with practice acquisitions and integrations.

Job Description

Lead technical discovery, due diligence, planning, implementation, validation, and post-transition stabilization for practice acquisitions, onboarding projects, and technology transitions. 
Lead and coordinate technical workstreams associated with practice acquisitions, facility relocations, network upgrades, Microsoft 365 migrations, and infrastructure modernization initiatives. 
Conduct onsite and remote assessments of practice environments, including Microsoft 365, internet connectivity, firewalls, switches, wireless access points, VPNs, servers, endpoints, voice services, cabling, security controls, and application dependencies. 
Develop and execute prioritized remediation plans that align acquired and existing practices with Integrated Dermatology network, security, Microsoft 365, endpoint, infrastructure, and documentation standards. 
Lead Microsoft 365 migration activities for acquired practices, including technical discovery, migration planning, domain and identity coordination, Exchange Online, OneDrive, SharePoint and Teams migration, cutover support, validation, and post-migration stabilization. 
Serve as the subject matter expert for SonicWall firewall technologies, including VPN connectivity, security policy design, content filtering, network segmentation, intrusion prevention, and secure remote access. 
Serve as the subject matter expert for Ubiquiti networking infrastructure, including switching, wireless networking, cloud management, configuration standards, performance optimization, and troubleshooting. 
Develop technical designs, bills of materials, project scopes, migration schedules, implementation checklists, validation plans, and post-transition support plans. 
Develop and maintain standard deployment configurations, implementation templates, site-readiness checklists, migration playbooks, and transition documentation to support repeatable acquisition and integration processes. 
Travel to practice and corporate locations to oversee implementations, resolve transition issues, validate company-standard configurations, and provide onsite technical leadership. 
Provide technical direction to managed service providers, internet carriers, cabling providers, equipment vendors, migration vendors, and implementation partners. 
Maintain site diagrams, inventories, circuit information, network documentation, configuration baselines, migration records, and operational handoff materials while providing technical guidance to Systems Administrators and IT Support Analysts.



Qualifications

Advanced experience configuring, administering, and troubleshooting SonicWall firewall and Ubiquiti switching and wireless solutions. 
Demonstrated experience leading acquisitions, practice transitions, infrastructure migrations, site integrations, or multi-location technology deployments. 
Experience assessing Microsoft 365 tenant environments and executing migrations involving Exchange Online, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams, domains, identities, licensing, and related data. 
Experience conducting technical site assessments and converting findings into remediation plans, project scopes, equipment requirements, migration plans, and implementation schedules. 
Strong knowledge of TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VPNs, VLANs, Wi-Fi, firewalls, network segmentation, internet circuits, and secure remote access. 
Experience coordinating internet carriers, cabling providers, managed service providers, equipment vendors, migration vendors, and onsite resources. 
Working knowledge of Microsoft 365, Entra ID, Intune, endpoint deployment, Windows infrastructure, identity lifecycle processes, and hybrid connectivity. 
Exceptional communication, relationship-building, and customer-service skills with the ability to effectively engage physicians, practice administrators, office managers, vendors, executive leadership, and technical teams. Ability to communicate technical concepts, project risks, implementation plans, and remediation recommendations clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences. 
Ability to manage concurrent transition projects, communicate risks and dependencies clearly, lead meetings, build stakeholder trust, and provide onsite technical leadership in environments with changing priorities.



Additional Information

Job Type: 

Full-time



Experience

6+ years designing, implementing, and supporting network, endpoint, Microsoft 365, site-infrastructure, and multi-location technology solutions. Experience leading Microsoft 365 migrations, practice transitions, acquisitions, infrastructure migrations, or site integrations is required. 



Education

Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field preferred. Equivalent advanced professional experience may be considered. 



Certifications/Licenses

SonicWall Network Security Administrator, Microsoft 365 certification, CompTIA Network+, CompTIA Security+, Ubiquiti UniFi certification, or comparable Microsoft, networking, and security certifications are preferred. 



Travel

Ability to travel up to 30% to support practice acquisitions, integrations, infrastructure projects, and onsite technical initiatives. Overnight travel may be required.

title: Associate Manager, Service Desk & Operations
desc:
Department/Team: Technology 
Salary: $56,000 - $66,000 (not negotiable) 
*typically, new hires are placed at the start of the salary range*
FLSA Status: Exempt 
Expected Start Date: ASAP 
Location: Miami Gardens, Florida 
Type: Hybrid (3 days on-site/2 remote) 
About Sandy Hook Promise  
Sandy Hook Promise (SHP) envisions a future where all children are free from school shootings and other acts of violence. As a national nonprofit organization, SHP’s mission is to educate and empower youth and adults to prevent violence in schools, homes, and communities. Creators of the lifesaving, evidence-informed Know the Signs prevention programs, SHP teaches the warning signs of someone who may be in crisis, socially isolated, or at-risk of hurting themselves or others and how to get help. SHP also advances school safety, youth mental health, and responsible gun ownership at the state and federal levels through nonpartisan policy and partnerships.    
 
SHP is led by several family members whose loved ones were killed in the tragic mass shooting at Sandy Hook Elementary School on December 14, 2012.    
Commitment to Belonging, Community, Engagement, and Respect  
SHP strives to ensure its culture and work environment reflect the values of belonging, community, engagement and respect.  We actively seek to understand and respond to the diverse perspectives and lived experiences of individuals across socioeconomic backgrounds, rural and urban communities, and diversity of thought, in addition to traditional protected categories. We are committed to ensuring that every SHP employee feels heard, valued, and a true sense of belonging.  SHP encourages individuals who share our commitment to these core values and to our mission to apply.   
Location 
We are a U.S.-based organization, and most team members work remotely from locations across the country unless otherwise specified. This role is a hybrid position that requires on-site attendance at our Miami Gardens, Florida office three days per week. 
To be considered, applicants must reside in the Miami-Dade County/Broward County area and be able to reliably commute to the office on designated in-person workdays. Team members are expected to make thoughtful travel decisions that balance cost, convenience, and sustainability. 
Location, Schedule, and Physical Requirements  
This is a full-time role that follows a hybrid work schedule based at our National Crisis Center in Miami, Florida. Applicants must reside within commuting distance of Miami, Florida. 
Physical Requirements  
Ability to lift 20–25 lbs. (ex., mail packages, office supplies, etc.).  
Ability to stand and walk around the office for short periods. 
Ability to operate standard office equipment (laptops, computers, copiers, scanners, postage machines, etc). 
About the Role 
The Associate Manager, Service Desk & Operations is a hands-on Tier 1/Tier 2 technology professional who independently owns day-to-day service desk operations, endpoint support activities, and assigned technology workstreams. This role is responsible for resolving routine technical issues with minimal supervision, exercising sound judgment regarding escalation, identifying opportunities to improve support processes, and ensuring a high-quality support experience for staff across the organization. 
The position focuses on responsive ticket management, accurate documentation, Windows endpoint support, and practical troubleshooting of Microsoft 365, internet/Wi-Fi connectivity, and Avaya Cloud Office. The Associate Manager supports SHP technology nationwide, including the deployment, management, and troubleshooting of laptops and related technology for remote employees. During scheduled on-site days in Miami, the role also provides hands-on support for workstations, peripherals, and office technology, while coordinating additional site visits and vendor support as needed. 
Job Responsibilities   
Service Desk & User Support 
Manage and resolve incidents and service requests in Freshservice or a comparable ITSM system; accurately categorize, prioritize, assign, track, and close tickets in accordance with service level agreements (SLAs).  
Troubleshoot Windows, Microsoft 365, account access, common SaaS issues, printers, peripherals, and remote-work tools.  
Document solutions consistently and contribute reusable fixes to the team knowledge base; identify incomplete tickets and follow up on unresolved requests.  
Maintain clear, timely ticket updates, troubleshooting histories, user communications, resolution notes, and escalation handoffs so another technician can understand and continue the work.  
Independently manage a portfolio of service desk responsibilities, identify recurring issues and support trends, recommend practical process improvements, and implement approved enhancements that improve the user experience, service quality, or operational efficiency. 
Endpoint Management & Device Lifecycle 
Prepare, deploy, troubleshoot, and recover Windows laptops and desktops, including shared workstations; provide hands-on diagnosis of hardware failures involving batteries, power, screens, keyboards, storage, docking stations, monitors, mice, headsets, webcams, printers, cables, adapters, and other computer accessories.  
Support Microsoft Intune enrollment, Windows Autopilot provisioning, Microsoft Entra device registration/join troubleshooting, configuration policies, updates, and application deployment. 
Investigate device compliance, sign-in, sync, connectivity, driver, and application installation problems; escalate complex configuration changes appropriately.  
Diagnose hardware failures, check warranty or extended-support coverage, open and manage repair cases with manufacturers or approved vendors, arrange shipping or on-site service, and keep users informed through repair, replacement, and return to service.  
Maintain accurate hardware inventory; coordinate secure data backup, device resets, replacements, shipping, returns, and recycling in accordance with policy. 
User Lifecycle, Microsoft 365 & SaaS 
Provision and deprovision user accounts, access, and licenses through approved onboarding/offboarding workflows.  
Support Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, Outlook, Microsoft 365 groups, and multifactor authentication.  
Provide first-line access and usability support for approved business applications and escalate application-specific configuration or data issues to designated owners. 
Documentation & Operations 
Write, maintain, and improve knowledge base articles, how-to guides, and repeatable troubleshooting instructions that are clear enough for colleagues and end users to follow.  
Partner with Sandy Hook staff and external vendors; proactively communicate status, expected timelines, workarounds, and next steps in plain language that nontechnical users can understand.  
Identify opportunities to strengthen support operations, documentation practices, ticket workflows, onboarding materials, or technology processes and proactively implement improvements within established guidelines. 
Must obtain the Microsoft 365 Certified: Endpoint Administrator Associate (MD-102) certification within one year of employment.  
SHP will support training and examination costs in accordance with its professional development policies. 
A commitment to SHP’s mission and values.  
Other duties identified as organizational needs.  
Desired Skills and Experience 
1-2 years of progressively responsible experience in IT service desk, desktop support, endpoint management, or technical support environments, including demonstrated ability to independently manage support tickets and resolve routine technical issues with limited supervision 
2+ years of experience in IT service desk, desktop support, endpoint management, or a related technical support role, with a demonstrated ability to independently manage support tickets, troubleshoot technical issues, document solutions, and coordinate hardware repair and replacement activities. 
Experience supporting Windows 10/11, Microsoft 365 applications, user access, and endpoint management through Microsoft Intune and Microsoft Entra ID, including device enrollment, application deployment, compliance review, and user/group administration. 
Experience working with ITSM platforms (e.g., Freshservice, Jira Service Management, or Zendesk) and external partners, including managed service providers (MSPs), internet service providers, and telecommunications vendors, to resolve incidents and service requests. 
Strong customer service, communication, documentation, troubleshooting, and prioritization skills, with the ability to independently resolve routine issues, exercise sound judgment, communicate effectively with nontechnical users, and contribute to process improvements. 
Preferred Experience/Qualifications (Not Required) 
Experience with Windows Autopilot, shared-device configurations, and advanced Microsoft Intune administration. 
Exposure to Meraki networking, Wi-Fi infrastructure, and vendor-supported network troubleshooting. 
Experience supporting remote and distributed workforces, nonprofit organizations, or service-oriented environments. 
CompTIA A+, Network+, Microsoft certifications, or related technical training.  
Microsoft 365 Certified: Endpoint Administrator Associate (MD-102) certification is a plus. 
Benefits and Salary Range  
The salary range for this position is $56,000 - $66,000. 
SHP uses a structured internal rubric to guide salary placement and ensure equitable pay. Typically, new hires are placed at the start of the salary range to ensure equity with current employees, and as a practice, we do not negotiate salaries.   
SHP offers a competitive benefits package, including: Unlimited PTO 
Flexible schedules 
Paid holidays and 10 days sick leave 
Paid parental leave 
Health, dental, and vision 
Employer paid life insurance and short- and long-term disability 
401k match 
Professional development stipend 
Wellness & mental health support 
Employer Paid Employee Assistance Program. 

Our organization operates within a distributed workforce, allowing for location flexibility across the country for most positions. We provide remote office support for all staff, which includes a laptop, home office reimbursement, monthly Wi-Fi reimbursement up to $40, and monthly cell phone reimbursement up to $50.

title: Senior Microsoft 365 Engineer
desc:
Senior Microsoft 365 Engineer


Location: College Station, TX (Hybrid – 2–3 days onsite per week)
Employment Type: Direct Hire


Position Overview
We are seeking an experienced Microsoft 365 Engineer to lead a major tenant-to-tenant migration and take long-term ownership of an organization's Microsoft 365 environment.


The organization is transitioning away from a shared technology environment and establishing its own independent Microsoft 365 tenant. This position will play a key role in planning and executing that separation, including migrating messaging, collaboration, identity, and endpoint services.


Following the migration, this individual will be responsible for the ongoing administration, security, optimization, and development of the Microsoft 365 platform.


This is a hands-on technical position with significant ownership and autonomy. The ideal candidate has personally performed complex Microsoft 365 migrations and is comfortable taking responsibility for both the initial transition and ongoing platform operations.


Key Responsibilities
-- Plan and execute a Microsoft 365 tenant-to-tenant migration, including Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, OneDrive, Teams, and associated identity services.
-- Manage technical migration activities, including discovery, tenant configuration, data migration, identity and domain transitions, cutover planning, and post-migration validation.
Support the transition of endpoint management and device configurations through Microsoft Intune.
-- Establish and maintain Microsoft 365 administration, security, governance, and operational standards.
-- Manage Entra ID, including identity synchronization, authentication, access controls, and Conditional Access policies.
-- Develop and maintain PowerShell scripts and automation to support migrations, administration, and ongoing operations.
-- Troubleshoot complex Microsoft 365 issues across messaging, collaboration, identity, and endpoint services.
-- Work with internal stakeholders and external technology partners during the transition, with responsibility for bringing ongoing platform management in-house.
-- Identify opportunities to improve platform reliability, security, performance, and the end-user experience.


Required Qualifications
-- Strong hands-on experience administering and engineering enterprise Microsoft 365 environments.
-- Demonstrated experience personally executing Microsoft 365 tenant-to-tenant migrations, including migration planning, technical execution, cutover, and validation.
-- Experience migrating and supporting Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, OneDrive, and Microsoft Teams.
-- Strong understanding of Entra ID (Azure AD), identity management, authentication, and Microsoft 365 tenant configuration.
-- Experience with Microsoft Intune and endpoint/device management.
-- Proficiency with PowerShell for Microsoft 365 administration, automation, and migration activities.
-- Experience working in environments with established security, compliance, and governance requirements.
-- Ability to work independently, troubleshoot complex issues, and take ownership of technical projects from planning through completion.


Preferred Qualifications
-- Experience with M365 migrations involving organizational separations, mergers, acquisitions, or divestitures.
-- Experience with migration tools such as Quest, BitTitan MigrationWiz, ShareGate, or similar platforms.
-- Familiarity with Exchange Hybrid environments and Microsoft Teams Phone.
-- Experience with Microsoft Defender, Purview, and related security and compliance capabilities.
-- Relevant Microsoft 365 or Azure certifications.


Why Consider This Opportunity?
This position offers the opportunity to take ownership of a significant Microsoft 365 transformation rather than simply maintain an existing environment.


You'll be involved in establishing an independent tenant, making key technical decisions, and building the foundation for how the organization manages Microsoft 365 moving forward.


The role offers meaningful technical ownership, direct involvement in a major migration, and the opportunity to help shape the organization's long-term Microsoft 365 strategy and operations.

desc:

Location: Marysville, OH

📍 Must be willing to work onsite in Marysville, OH
🚫 W2 ONLY — No C2C, No 3rd Parties


Position Summary
We are seeking an experienced Senior Mobile Device Management (MDM) Engineer to manage, support, and optimize enterprise mobile device platforms using Microsoft Intune, Apple Business Manager, and Android Enterprise.
This role focuses on supporting company-managed iPhones, iPads, and rugged Android handheld scanners used across manufacturing and distribution environments. The ideal candidate brings strong expertise in mobile device enrollment, configuration, compliance, application management, OS deployment, and advanced troubleshooting.
This individual will serve as a Level 3 technical escalation resource, ensuring mobile devices remain secure, compliant, operational, and capable of supporting business-critical applications. Engineer, administer, and support enterprise Mobile Device Management (MDM) platforms using Microsoft Intune
Resolve escalated iOS/iPadOS and Android device issues, including enrollment, compliance, application functionality, and connectivity
Manage Microsoft Intune and Apple Business Manager configurations, policies, groups, and device actions

Package, deploy, configure, and maintain public, private, and line-of-business mobile applications

Identify compliance gaps and drive remediation activities
Implement configuration changes and deployments through ServiceNow change management
Develop and maintain technical documentation, runbooks, knowledge articles, and status reports
Use scripting and automation to improve device management, reporting, and operational efficiency

Automation & Reporting: Using PowerShell and Microsoft Graph to support reporting, device administration, and process improvements

5+ years of Mobile Device Management (MDM) experience

title: Technology Operations Specialist
desc:
Position: Technology Operations Specialist
Location: New Albany, OH (Hybrid)


Position Description:
In this Hybrid role reporting to our New Albany, OH office, the Technology Operations Specialist is responsible for supporting and maintaining Mission Essential's enterprise technology environment. This role provides end-user support, administers Microsoft 365 and Azure services, supports cybersecurity operations, manages endpoint technologies, and participates in the implementation and support of business systems and technology initiatives. This position serves as a technical generalist within a small, highly collaborative IT organization. The Technology Operations Specialist is expected to support all aspects of IT operations, ranging from end-user support and device management to cloud administration, cybersecurity monitoring, compliance initiatives, and project implementation.


The successful employee must demonstrate strong technical proficiency, excellent customer service skills, sound judgment, and a team-first mentality while supporting the organization's mission and operational objectives.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:


End-User Support
Provide Tier 1, Tier 2, and Tier 3 support for employees located both remotely and on-site.
Troubleshoot and resolve hardware, software, operating system, networking, printing, mobile device, and application issues.
Configure, deploy, and maintain desktops, laptops, mobile devices, and peripherals.
Support employee onboarding, offboarding, account provisioning, and access management activities.
Maintain technical documentation, procedures, and knowledge base resources.
Provide exceptional customer service and maintain professional communication during all support interactions.
Cloud & Systems Administration
Administer Microsoft 365 services including Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint Online, OneDrive, Entra ID, and related cloud services.
Manage user accounts, licensing, permissions, and service configurations.
Support Azure and Azure Government resources including subscriptions, resource groups, storage, networking, security controls, certificates, and identity services.
Assist with administration of GCC High environments and cloud-based business applications.
Monitor platform health and assist with operational improvements.
Administer Microsoft Intune and endpoint management platforms.
Manage Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android devices.
Configure and maintain security baselines, compliance policies, device configurations, and application deployments.
Support endpoint security, patch management, mobile device administration, and device lifecycle activities.
Security & Compliance
Monitor, investigate, and respond to alerts generated by SIEM, MDR, EDR, and other cybersecurity platforms.
Support security operations utilizing technologies such as Microsoft Sentinel, Microsoft Defender, Rapid7, and related security solutions.
Assist with incident response activities, cybersecurity investigations, containment efforts, and remediation actions.
Participate in vulnerability management, security reviews, and risk reduction activities.
Support compliance initiatives including CMMC, NIST 800-171, HIPAA, GDPR, and FedRAMP where applicable.
Assist with audits, evidence collection, documentation, and security assessments.
Vendor & Project Coordination
Participate in technology projects, migrations, upgrades, and system implementations.
Work with vendors and business stakeholders to resolve issues and support operational requirements.
Assist with technology evaluations, procurement activities, and asset management processes.
Maintain accurate system inventories and technical records.
Team & Operational Support
Collaborate with other IT team members to support organizational technology needs.
Share knowledge and cross-train on systems and technologies as needed.
Balance operational support responsibilities with project-related assignments.
Assist with critical incidents, outages, maintenance activities, and urgent business needs that may occur outside normal business hours.
Participate in after-hours maintenance and support when required to maintain operational continuity.
Perform other duties as assigned.


Minimum Qualifications:
Associate’s degree in information technology, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or related discipline, or equivalent experience.
Minimum three years of enterprise IT support, systems administration, cloud administration, or cybersecurity experience.
Experience administering Microsoft 365 environments.
Experience supporting Azure environments.
Experience with Microsoft Intune and endpoint management technologies.
Experience supporting Windows desktop and server platforms.
Experience with PowerShell scripting and automation.
Working knowledge of networking fundamentals including DNS, DHCP, VPN, LAN, and wireless technologies.
Working knowledge of SIEM, MDR, EDR, incident response, and cybersecurity best practices.
Ability to obtain and maintain a Secret security clearance if required.


Desired Qualifications:
Security+, Network+, Microsoft Security Operations Analyst, Microsoft Identity and Access Administrator Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate, Microsoft Endpoint Administrator or equivalent certifications.


Other Notes:
On-call availability for end-users to perform networking, desktop support, systems administration, and security duties.
Must be available to work flexible hours (weekends, after hours, etc.) if required maintaining normal system operation.
Occasional travel to CONUS or OCONUS locations for support of off-site staff.

desc:
Title: Senior Technical Support Engineer
Location: Downtown Boston, Financial District | In Office - Monday Through Friday
Budget: $95K to $110K Based On Experience + Bonus
Full-Time | Exempt


We are partnering with a growing organization seeking a Senior Technical Support Engineer to lead enterprise endpoint engineering while providing high-level technology support to executive leadership.


This is a hands-on, highly visible role responsible for the strategy, engineering, administration, and continuous improvement of the company's enterprise endpoint environment. The position will oversee Windows, macOS, and mobile device management, endpoint security, automation, provisioning, patching, and lifecycle management. In addition to owning endpoint engineering initiatives, this individual will serve as a trusted technology partner to the executive leadership team, providing white-glove support for C-suite executives, board meetings, executive offsites, and other high-profile business events. The ideal candidate brings deep technical expertise in endpoint management, strong communication skills, executive presence, and the ability to balance strategic engineering initiatives with hands-on technical support.


Please note: This position requires working on-site at the company's Boston office Monday through Friday. Candidates must live within commuting distance. Fully remote work is not available. Travel may be required to support executive offsites and business events.


Key Responsibilities
Enterprise Endpoint Engineering
Own the enterprise endpoint engineering strategy, roadmap, and lifecycle management across Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android devices.
Lead the design, implementation, administration, and ongoing improvement of enterprise endpoint management platforms, including Microsoft Intune, MECM, Autopilot, Addigy, or similar technologies.
Develop standardized device provisioning, imaging, deployment, configuration, and lifecycle management processes.
Oversee endpoint security, configuration policies, Group Policy, encryption, compliance, patch management, and vulnerability remediation.
Develop PowerShell scripts and automation solutions to reduce manual processes and improve operational efficiency.
Establish endpoint standards, technical documentation, governance, and operational best practices.
Partner with Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, Networking, and IT leadership to improve endpoint security, reliability, and the overall employee technology experience.
Lead endpoint-related projects, including hardware refreshes, office expansions, migrations, and enterprise technology deployments.
Identify recurring technical issues, perform root cause analysis, and implement long-term solutions.
Executive Technology Support
Serve as the senior technology resource and trusted IT partner for executive leadership.
Provide high-touch, white-glove technical support to C-suite executives.
Support board meetings, executive offsites, conferences, leadership retreats, and other high-profile business events.
Travel as needed to support executive leadership and ensure seamless technology operations.
Oversee executive conference room technology, audio/visual systems, collaboration platforms, hybrid meetings, and presentation support.
Operational Leadership
Provide technical leadership and mentorship to Desktop Support personnel.
Serve as the senior escalation point for complex endpoint and end-user technology issues.
Establish service standards, KPIs, operational metrics, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Partner with IT leadership on endpoint strategy, budgeting, technology roadmaps, and vendor evaluations.
Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency through automation, standardization, and technology modernization.
Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Management Information Systems, or a related field. Equivalent professional experience will be considered.
6+ years of progressive experience in endpoint engineering, desktop engineering, IT operations, or enterprise end-user technology support.
3+ years of direct experience providing executive-level, white-glove technology support in a corporate environment.
Strong experience managing Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android endpoints, including provisioning, imaging, software deployment, patching, automation, and lifecycle management.
Hands-on experience with enterprise endpoint management platforms such as Microsoft Intune, MECM, Autopilot, Addigy, or comparable technologies.
Experience developing endpoint standards, policies, governance, and operational processes.
Strong understanding of endpoint security, device compliance, encryption, endpoint hardening, vulnerability remediation, and identity/access management.
Experience supporting Microsoft 365 and modern enterprise collaboration platforms.
Demonstrated scripting and automation experience using PowerShell or similar technologies.
Ability to lead complex troubleshooting efforts, perform root cause analysis, and implement lasting technical improvements.
Experience supporting executive leadership, board meetings, conference rooms, and high-profile business events is strongly preferred.
Familiarity with ITSM frameworks, technical documentation, and cross-functional IT environments.
Relevant certifications such as Microsoft 365 Endpoint Administrator Associate, CompTIA A+, Network+, Security+, or ITIL Foundation are preferred.
Experience supporting distributed, multi-site, retail, hospitality, restaurant, or franchise-based environments is a plus.
Additional Skills
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage competing priorities.
Excellent communication and presentation skills, including the ability to interact confidently with executives and technical teams.
Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build collaborative relationships across all levels of an organization.
Ability to provide technical leadership, mentor team members, and influence technology decisions.
Curious, proactive, and interested in continuously learning and improving existing processes.
Comfortable working in a fast-paced, evolving environment while maintaining a high level of service.
Compensation & Benefits
Base Salary: $95,000–$110,000, depending on experience and qualifications.
Eligible for an annual corporate bonus based on company and individual performance.
Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance.
401(k) with employer matching.
Employee stock purchase plan.

Additional wellness, childcare, and employee engagement benefits.

title: Principal Battery Systems Engineer
desc:
ON.energy is setting the standard for large load interconnection. ON’s patented AI UPS™ is a medium-voltage UPS that serves as a firewall, protecting the data center from the grid, and the grid from the data center. With multiple gigawatts currently under construction, we are enabling grid-safe data centers. 
 Principal Battery Systems Engineer 
Role Overview 
We're looking for a Principal Engineer to set the technical direction for our BESS product line and to own the product roadmap across multiple concurrent development cycles. This is the senior technical voice on the product team: you'll architect new products, resolve the hardest engineering trade-offs, set the engineering standards others work to, and represent ON.energy's product engineering externally — to vendors, customers, certifying bodies, and the broader industry. You should be comfortable operating with minimal direction, holding the bar on technical quality, and moving multiple product cycles forward in parallel without losing the thread on any of them. 
What You'll Own 
Architecture & Technical Direction 
Set the architecture for the BESS product line and own the technical roadmap across multiple concurrent product cycles. 
Make the hard trade-off calls — cost vs reliability, performance vs lead time, standardization vs customization — and document the reasoning so future decisions inherit context. 
Define the engineering standards, design rules, and review gates that other engineers on the team work to. Own the product-engineering bar. 
Approve major design changes; act as the final technical authority on the change baseline. 
Multi-Product Development 
Run multiple product development cycles in parallel — concept through prototype, FAT, field deployment, and revision — without losing depth on any of them. 
Drive cycle cadence: decide what ships when, where the technical risk lives, what gets parallelized vs sequenced. 
Identify and execute the next-generation product moves — higher voltage class, alternate chemistries, new form factors — ahead of customer demand. 
Detailed Engineering Depth 
Personally own the hardest pieces of work: novel architectures, first-of-kind designs, advanced component sizing (fuse coordination, busbar thermal optimization, protection coordination across cascaded systems), cabinet thermal modeling, and complex protection schemes. 
Review and approve detailed engineering drawings — SLDs, GAs, schematics, panel layouts — at the level required to sign off, not just consult. 
Vendor & Supply Chain Strategy 
Own the strategic relationships with key vendors — battery, PCS, BoP. Decide the architecture of those relationships: sole-source vs dual-source, co-development depth, IP boundaries. 
Set the technical qualification process used by the team and enforce it. Run the highest-stakes design reviews and resolve the highest-stakes vendor escalations personally. 
Engineering Leadership & Mentorship 
Mentor and develop other engineers on the team. Build their technical judgment, not just their throughput. 
Run design reviews. Lead post-mortems on field issues and turn them into product changes. 
Set the cadence and quality bar for ECR/ECN, FMEA, design reviews, and product handoff. 
External & Cross-Functional Representation 
Represent ON.energy's product engineering externally — customer technical reviews, vendor escalations, industry working groups, certifying bodies, conferences. 
Partner with the commercial team on the most technically complex pursuits and proposals — proposing architectures, defending positions, structuring technical exhibits in LTSAs and supply agreements. 
Brief leadership on technical risk and product roadmap decisions. 
Required Qualifications 
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Electronics, or a closely related technical field. MS preferred. 
10+ years of hands-on engineering experience in BESS, power electronics, UPS, or comparable mission-critical industrial power systems, with a demonstrated record of operating with minimal direction in a senior technical role. 
Owned multiple product development cycles end-to-end and independently. You've personally designed and integrated a BESS at the system level, from engineering through commissioning and into live operation, not just handed it off at FAT, and the products are still in the field. 
Architecture-level decision authority on previous BESS equipment. You've made the trade-off calls others built around, not just executed someone else's architecture. 
Deep, demonstrable skill in detailed component sizing — fuse coordination, busbar sizing, protection device selection, thermal sizing for enclosed cabinets — at the level required to sign off on production designs. 
Fluency producing and reviewing SLDs, GAs, schematics, and panel layouts; expert with AutoCAD or equivalent E-CAD; comfortable across mechanical drawings. 
Strong track record running strategic vendor relationships through design, FAT, serial production, and post-deployment escalation. 
Excellent written and verbal communication — specs, technical positions, design review leadership, board-level briefings. 
Willing to travel up to 25–30% for FAT inspections, site commissioning, customer engagements, and vendor reviews. 
Preferred 
Direct experience with data center / UPS / mission-critical power or utility-scale BESS at the architecture level. 
Active involvement in standards bodies (UL, IEC, NFPA, IEEE working groups, CSA TC committees) or technical conference contributions. 
Patents, peer-reviewed publications, or other evidence of recognized technical depth in the field. 
PE license. 
Familiarity with UL 9540 / 9540A, NFPA 855, IEC 62619, IEEE 1547, NEC Article 706, plus the relevant codes for target markets. 
Experience standing up or scaling structured PLM, ECR/ECN, and design-review processes. 
Multi-domain depth — BMS / cell engineering, PCS / power electronics, thermal / mechanical — alongside the EE core.

title: Telecommunications Architect
desc:
Summary


The Telecommunications Architect designs, engineers and supports Great HealthWorks' voice and contact center technology end to end. The role carries two equally weighted areas of ownership: the Company's self-hosted open-source voice platform built on Kazoo, FreeSWITCH and Kamailio across a Linux server estate; and the NICE InContact (CXone) cloud contact center, including script design and tier-3 support. A third core responsibility bridges the two: managing and maintaining the API integrations that connect the voice platform, the contact center, the Omilia speech IVR and the in-house GHW-Pay SMS application into a single customer experience. This is an architect-level position as much as an engineering one. Given the age of the current voice platform, the incumbent is expected to assess it, define a modern target state, and lead its redesign or rebuild. The Architect sets technical standards across the communications estate and provides technical direction to the telecom administrator and the contact center managed services partner, without direct reports. Clear, current technical documentation is a required deliverable of the role, not an afterthought.


Key Responsibilities 


Voice Platform and Infrastructure: Open Source


Own the architecture of the Company's voice platform. Assess the current Kazoo (2600Hz), FreeSWITCH, Kamailio, RabbitMQ, BigCouch/CouchDB and HAProxy environment, define a modern target state, and design the rebuild where platform age, supportability or business need requires it
Lead the technical design, build, migration and cutover of voice platform modernization projects, including proof of concept, capacity and resiliency planning, testing strategy and rollback planning
Administer, patch and upgrade the voice platform and its supporting application components, partnering with the Network Operations team, who own server operating system lifecycle, patching and hardening
Author, test and troubleshoot FreeSWITCH XML dialplans, Sofia SIP profiles and gateways, and Kamailio routing configuration
Operate the Erlang/OTP services underpinning the platform (Kazoo, RabbitMQ, BigCouch), including node and cluster health, distribution and service recovery
Maintain IP phone provisioning infrastructure, device configuration templates and firmware distribution
Create IVR and auto-attendant call routes and perform IVR development on the open-source voice platform


Contact Center Platform: NICE InContact (CXone)


Design, configure and implement contact center solutions and scripts in NICE InContact (CXone) Studio, including routing logic, queues, skills, prompts, data dips, agent states and disposition handling
Build and maintain callback, overflow, after-hours and holiday routing, points of contact, and business hours profiles
Provide tier-3 support, root-cause analysis and resolution for contact center issues escalated by the telecom administrator or managed services partner
Build and maintain contact center reporting, historical data extracts and dashboards for business stakeholders
Manage contact center release, feature and configuration changes, including regression testing prior to production release
Support the Omilia speech IVR (sIVR) fronting NICE InContact, including call and data hand-off and fault isolation across the Omilia-to-NICE boundary


Integrations and APIs


Manage and maintain the REST API integrations between the contact center, the voice platform, the Omilia speech IVR and the in-house GHW-Pay SMS application
Maintain automation and integration scripts in Python and Bash, version controlled in Git with GitLab CI pipelines
Manage and support authentication, webhooks, callbacks, retry logic and error handling across integrated platforms
Partner with the AppDev team on interface contracts, change coordination and defect triage for the internally built GHW-Pay application
Trace a customer interaction end to end across the speech IVR, contact center routing, agent desktop, call detail records and SMS confirmation, and identify and resolve the point of failure


Documentation, Monitoring and Change Management


Produce and maintain current architecture documentation, call flow and network diagrams, configuration standards and operational runbooks for every supported platform; documentation is a required deliverable of each change and project
Maintain and update voice portals for carriers including call routes for DIDs and 8XX, number porting and SIP trunk turn-up
Configure alerts and monitoring for telephony systems, applications and services, and monitor QoS, jitter, packet loss, dropped calls, service levels and availability to deliver approved service levels to the business
Operate call detail recording and reporting across the voice and contact center platforms
Perform load, failover and pre-change validation testing using SIPp and equivalent tooling
Work within established configuration and change management policies to ensure awareness, approval and success of changes made to the communications infrastructure
Participate in an on-call rotation supporting a 24x7 production voice and contact center environment


Escalation, Vendor and Project Support


Serve as the final internal escalation point for complex voice and contact center issues that cannot be resolved by the telecom administrator or the managed services partner
Monitor the telecom service ticket queue in InvGate for escalated service requests
Set technical and configuration standards for the communications estate, provide technical direction to the telecom administrator and the contact center managed services partner, and review their work for quality and adherence to those standards
Serve as liaison to vendors and carriers on all aspects of the business communication systems
Work with business users to develop and implement acceptance test plans to ensure that solutions meet customer requirements and expectations
Other related duties as assigned by management


Required Qualifications 
Minimum Education and Experience


Bachelor’s Degree in an IT related program, or equivalent professional experience
8 + years of professional, related experience
Demonstrable hands-on experience in both areas of this role: open-source VoIP platform engineering on Linux, and cloud contact center administration and scripting
Demonstrated experience designing, rebuilding or migrating a production voice platform, not solely administering one
Previous experience supporting call center environments required
Previous experience managing or supporting REST API integrations between communications platforms required
Previous experience inspecting network traffic from a voice perspective a plus
Experience setting technical standards and providing technical direction to internal administrators and managed service partners
Experience with formal change management
Relevant certification is a plus (NICE CXone, SIP School SSCA, RHCSA or Linux Foundation LFCS, 2600Hz Kazoo)


Knowledge, Skills and Abilities


Voice Platform and Open Source
Working knowledge of Kazoo (2600Hz), FreeSWITCH and Kamailio
Ability to architect and document a target-state voice platform, including migration, cutover and rollback planning
Linux administration at the application layer across RHEL-family and Debian-family distributions
Knowledge of RabbitMQ, CouchDB/BigCouch and MariaDB in a production voice environment
Ability to read SIP messaging, and working knowledge of SDP, RTP/SRTP, NAT traversal, codecs and T.38 fax
Knowledge of Wireshark or similar products required


Contact Center
Working knowledge of NICE InContact (CXone), including Studio script development, routing, skill and queue design
Knowledge of speech or conversational IVR platforms and their integration with a cloud contact center (Omilia or equivalent)
Ability to build contact center reporting and interpret operational and service level metrics


Integration and Automation
Working knowledge of REST APIs, JSON, and authentication methods including OAuth 2.0, tokens and API keys
Scripting and automation ability in Python and Bash, with version control in Git


General
Knowledge of voice networking fundamentals including QoS, VLANs, multicast, DNS and SRV records, and NTP
Strong technical documentation discipline. The ability to produce and maintain architecture diagrams, call flow documentation, configuration standards and operational runbooks is a core requirement of this role


Physical/Work Environment/Expectations


While performing duties of job, incumbent is occasionally required to:
Operate in a professional office environment
